summary.title: The Reactive Manifesto
summary.one_liner: Reactive Systems are software systems that are Responsive, Resilient, Elastic and Message Driven, and the manifesto explains why these four properties matter for modern architecture.
keywords: how to build scalable fault-tolerant software
takeaways: Reactive Systems are defined by four properties: Responsive, Resilient, Elastic and Message Driven.
Resilience comes from replication, containment, isolation and delegating recovery to external components.
Elasticity requires designs without contention points or central bottlenecks, so components can be sharded or replicated.
Asynchronous, explicit message passing provides loose coupling, location transparency, load management and back-pressure.
Reactive properties should be applied at every level of scale so that systems stay composable.
summary.summary: The Reactive Manifesto argues that organisations are independently converging on similar patterns for robust, flexible software because application demands (millisecond response times, cloud clusters, petabyte data) have outgrown older architectures. It defines Reactive Systems by four properties: Responsive (consistent, timely replies), Resilient (staying responsive through failure via containment and delegation), Elastic (scaling resources with workload without bottlenecks), and Message Driven (asynchronous, location-transparent message passing with back-pressure). The page is a short, principle-level statement with no code or implementation details, and it notes that these properties should hold at every level of scale so systems compose.
